date:agrippa-and-bernice-meet-festus@a8f.note: No year in the text. Set after Festus succeeds Felix (24.27) and the king comes to Caesarea (25.13). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-appeals-to-caesar@a8fc17.note: No year in the text. Set after Festus takes office (24.27, 25.1). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-arrested-in-the-temple@06daca.note: No year in the text. The arrest comes before Felix's two years (24.27). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-gives-his-testimony@06daca.note: No year in the text. Given right after the arrest, from the castle stairs (21.40, 22.1). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-goes-before-agrippa@a8fc17.note: No year in the text. Set the day after Agrippa's request (25.22-23), after Festus takes office. The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-goes-before-the-council@06daca.note: No year in the text. Set on the morrow after the arrest and testimony (22.30). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-sent-to-felix@cd5d4b.note: No year in the text. Paul is held under Felix for two years (24.27). The 56-58 range depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:paul-visits-elders-in-jerusalem@06d.note: No year in the text. Set the day after arrival in Jerusalem (21.17-18). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:the-conspiracy-to-kill-paul@06daca.note: No year in the text. Set the morning after the night vision (23.11-12). The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:voyage-from-miletus-to-jerusalem@06.note: No year in the text. The voyage ends with arrival at Jerusalem (21.15-17), before the arrest. The year depends on dating outside Scripture.

occurred-at:paul-appeals-to-caesar>caesa.note: Matched 25.1 is the trip to Jerusalem. Festus hears the case at Caesarea (25.6), where Paul appeals (25.10-11).

occurred-at:paul-gives-his-testimony>jer.note: Jerusalem is not named in 22.1-2. He speaks from the castle stairs in the uproar at Jerusalem (21.31, 21.40).

occurred-at:paul-goes-before-agrippa>cae.note: Caesarea is not named in 25.23. Festus and Agrippa are at Caesarea (25.6, 25.13), where the hearing takes place.

occurred-at:paul-goes-before-the-council.note: Jerusalem is not named here. The chief priests' council meets in Jerusalem, where the castle and uproar are (21.31, 22.30).

occurred-at:paul-sent-to-felix>caesarea_.note: Matched 23.23 is only an order to go. They come to Caesarea and present Paul to the governor (23.33-34).

occurred-at:paul-visits-elders-in-jerusa.note: Matched nothing. They come to Jerusalem (21.17), and the next day Paul goes in to James and the elders (21.18).

occurred-at:the-conspiracy-to-kill-paul>.note: Jerusalem is not named. The plotters go to the chief priests and elders and ask for Paul to be brought down (23.14-15).

occurred-at:voyage-from-miletus-to-jerus.note: They sail past Cyprus and leave it on the left hand (21.3) without landing. The text shows passing by, not a stop.
Matched 21.4 is at Tyre. The journey ends when they go up to Jerusalem (21.15, 21.17).
Judea is not named in the voyage. Jerusalem, where it ends, lies in Judea. The text uses Judaea only at 21.10 and 26.20.

participated-in:agabus_107>voyage-from-m.note: Agabus comes down while they stay at Caesarea and acts there (21.10-11). He is not on the voyage itself.

participated-in:ananias_260>paul-sent-to.note: Ananias accuses Paul before Felix (24.1), after the transfer (23.23-35). Counts only if the Felix hearing is part of this event.

participated-in:bernice_482>paul-goes-be.note: Bernice enters the hearing place with Agrippa (25.23) but does not speak. Present, not acting.

participated-in:drusilla_1024>paul-sent-.note: Drusilla comes with Felix to the hearing (24.24) but does not speak or act. Counts only if the Felix hearing is part of this event.

participated-in:felix_1257>paul-sent-to-.note: Matched 23.24 is the order to bring Paul to him. Felix reads the letter and orders Paul kept (23.34-35).

participated-in:luke_1836>paul-visits-el.note: Luke is not named. The 'we' narrator goes up with Paul and goes in to James (21.15, 21.18). Naming him Luke is tradition, not the text.

participated-in:luke_1836>voyage-from-mi.note: Luke is not named. The 'we' narrator travels with Paul's company (21.1, 21.8). Naming him Luke is tradition, not the text.

participated-in:mnason_2102>voyage-from-.note: Disciples of Caesarea bring Mnason along to Jerusalem, and he hosts them (21.16). He is not on the sea leg.

participated-in:paul_2479>paul-appeals-t.note: Matched 25.2 is the accusation. Paul makes the appeal himself (25.10-11).

participated-in:paul_2479>paul-arrested-.note: Matched 21.29 is background. Paul is seized in the temple (21.30) and bound with chains (21.33).

participated-in:paul_2479>paul-gives-his.note: Matched 21.37 is his request to speak. He gives the defence from the stairs (22.1-21).

participated-in:paul_2479>paul-sent-to-f.note: Matched 23.24 is an order. Paul is taken by night to Antipatris and presented to the governor (23.31-33).

participated-in:paul_2479>the-conspiracy.note: Paul is the target (23.12). He acts by sending his nephew with word to the chief captain (23.16-17).

participated-in:paul_2479>voyage-from-mi.note: Matched 21.4 is at Tyre. Paul's company travels on to Caesarea and goes up to Jerusalem (21.8, 21.15).

participated-in:philip_2347>voyage-from-.note: Philip hosts them at Caesarea (21.8), a stop on the way. He is not on the voyage itself.

participated-in:portius_2367>agrippa-and.note: Agrippa and Bernice come to salute Festus (25.13), and he tells the king about Paul (25.14).

participated-in:portius_2367>paul-appeal.note: Festus offers Paul a trial at Jerusalem (25.9) and answers his appeal (25.12).

participated-in:portius_2367>paul-goes-b.note: At Festus's command Paul is brought forth, and Festus addresses the company (25.23-24).

participated-in:tertullus_2844>paul-sent.note: Tertullus accuses Paul before Felix (24.1), after the transfer (23.23-35). Counts only if the Felix hearing is part of this event.

visited:ananias_260>caesarea_266@144715.note: Caesarea is not named in 24.1. He descends with the elders to the governor, who holds Paul at Caesarea (23.35).

visited:ananias_260>jerusalem_636@57741d.note: Jerusalem is not named in 23.2. The high priest presides over the council that meets in Jerusalem (22.30).

visited:drusilla_1024>caesarea_266@632e6.note: Caesarea is not named in 24.24. Felix hears Paul with Drusilla where he holds Paul (23.35).

visited:felix_1257>caesarea_266@5a8922.note: Paul and the letter are delivered to the governor at Caesarea (23.33-34).

visited:mnason_2102>caesarea_266@72bbda.note: Caesarean disciples bring Mnason along. The text does not say he lives in Caesarea.

visited:mnason_2102>jerusalem_636@923072.note: They lodge with Mnason on arrival (21.16-17). Jerusalem is the arrival place but is not named in 21.16.

visited:mnason_2102>judea_657@6e89ef.note: Judea is not named. Jerusalem, where they lodge with him, lies in Judea.

visited:portius_2367>caesarea_266@8828a5.note: Festus orders Paul kept at Caesarea and goes down there himself (25.4, 25.6).

visited:tertullus_2844>caesarea_266@5f0d.note: Caesarea is not named in 24.1. He accuses Paul before the governor, who holds Paul at Caesarea (23.35).
